name: Christopher Cabaldon
title: California State Senator, Chair of the Senate Privacy, Digital Technologies and Consumer Protections Committee
district: California State Senate District 3 (Wine Country, the Delta, North Bay, and Sacramento Valley, including West Sacramento)
years_of_service: December 2, 2024–present (first term). Cabaldon's Senate service is short relative to many colleagues; before the Senate he spent 22 years as Mayor of West Sacramento (1998–2020). (Source: official Senate biography, sd03.senate.ca.gov/biography; Wikipedia, Christopher Cabaldon.)
background: Cabaldon earned a bachelor's degree in environmental economics from UC Berkeley, where he served as student body vice president, and a master's degree in public policy and administration from California State University, Sacramento, as a member of its founding class. Early in his career he was, at age 24, chief consultant and staff director to the California State Assembly's Higher Education Committee, and he also served as legislative director for the University of California Students Association. (Source: official Senate biography, sd03.senate.ca.gov/biography; Wikipedia, Christopher Cabaldon.)

Cabaldon was elected Mayor of West Sacramento in 1998 and served for 22 years, through 2020, making him the longest-serving mayor in the city's history. Under his leadership the city won the U.S. Conference of Mayors' 'America's Most Livable Small City' award and launched nation-first local initiatives including universal preschool and 'West Sacramento Home Run,' a program giving kindergartners college savings accounts, tuition-free community college, and automatic scholarship letters; the city also pursued affordable-housing, personal-mobility-transit, urban-farm, and flood-protection initiatives during his tenure. A state highway was renamed 'Christopher Cabaldon Parkway' in his honor. (Source: official Senate biography, sd03.senate.ca.gov/biography; Wikipedia, Christopher Cabaldon.)

Beyond the mayor's office, Cabaldon served as Vice Chancellor of the California Community Colleges system from 1997 to 2003, was CEO of EdVoice, a nonprofit education-advocacy organization, and held education and environment appointments under five California governors. He was a tenured faculty member at Sacramento State, holding the Hazel Cramer Endowed Chair (appointed 2019) and teaching design thinking, public-sector prototyping, and state/local government and urban economics. Nationally, he chaired the U.S. Conference of Mayors' Jobs, Education & Workforce Committee and was the inaugural chair of the national LGBTQ Mayors Alliance. He is the first Filipino American elected to the California State Senate and the first LGBTQ senator elected from north of San Francisco and Stockton. (Source: official Senate biography, sd03.senate.ca.gov/biography.)

Cabaldon ran for the open Senate District 3 seat in 2024, advancing from the March 2024 top-two primary with 26.6% of the vote (ahead of fellow Democrat Rozzana Verder-Aliga at 20.5%) and winning the November 2024 general election with 62.6% (277,092 votes) against Republican Thom Bogue's 37.4%. He was sworn in on December 2, 2024. (Source: Wikipedia, Christopher Cabaldon; this profile's authors were unable to load Ballotpedia's Christopher Cabaldon page, which returned no retrievable content on repeated attempts, so this election detail rests on Wikipedia rather than Ballotpedia.)
committee_memberships: Chair, Senate Privacy, Digital Technologies and Consumer Protections Committee
Member, Senate Natural Resources and Water Committee
voting_record_highlights: SB 417 (2025–2026), the Veterans and Affordable Housing Bond Act of 2026: Cabaldon was a Senate principal coauthor (lead authors were Sen. Monique Limón and Assemblymember Robert Rivas). It cleared the Senate concurrence vote 29–2 and was signed by Gov. Newsom on June 25, 2026 as Chapter 16, Statutes of 2026, placing a $10 billion general-obligation bond for veterans and affordable housing before voters as Proposition 1 on the November 2026 ballot. The ballot outcome itself is not yet known and is not counted as a past measure here; full detail on the measure is covered separately in the Proposition 1 file. (Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill status for SB 417.)

SB 5 (2025–2026), which would have excluded farmland enrolled in Williamson Act or farmland security zone contracts from tax-increment diversion to Enhanced Infrastructure Financing Districts and Community Revitalization and Investment Areas: Cabaldon was the sole/lead author. It passed both houses (Senate September 9, 2025; Assembly September 8, 2025) but was vetoed by Gov. Newsom on October 6, 2025; Newsom's veto message said the bill 'inappropriately reduces the ability of local agencies to choose how and where to use' existing infrastructure-financing tools. The veto was sustained March 2, 2026. (Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill status for SB 5.)

SB 226 (2025–2026), amending Government Code Section 53369.3 to let infrastructure revitalization financing districts finance entertainment or sports facilities as part of authorized commercial/industrial financing: Cabaldon was the lead Senate author with Assemblymember Cecilia Aguiar-Curry as principal coauthor. It passed the Assembly August 20, 2026 and the Senate August 30, 2026, and was enrolled and presented to the Governor on September 8, 2026; as of this profile's last update (September 22, 2026) it remains pending gubernatorial action, so its final outcome is not yet verifiable and it is not listed under past measures authored below. (Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill status/text for SB 226.)

Given Cabaldon's short Senate tenure (sworn in December 2024, in his first term), his authored-bill record is comparatively limited next to longer-serving colleagues; the Senate's own legislation page for him also lists SB 226, SB 438, SB 486, SB 640, SB 719, SB 744, SB 790 (education), SB 772 (housing/transportation), SB 299 (government efficiency), and SB 278, SB 339, SB 351 (healthcare), SB 514, SB 539, SB 650 (natural resources) among his 2025–2026 authored or coauthored bills; this profile was not able to verify final outcomes for most of these within its research budget. (Source: sd03.senate.ca.gov/legislation.)
attendance: No individually published floor-attendance or voting-participation record for Senator Cabaldon was found. The California State Senate does not publish a per-member attendance scorecard; the only public records located are bill-by-bill roll-call votes at leginfo.legislature.ca.gov, which is what the voting-record entries above are drawn from. An attempt to locate a CalMatters Digital Democracy legislator profile for Cabaldon (which for some legislators tracks bill-passage counts and vote-alignment percentages, though not attendance) returned no valid page during this research; his absence from that tool likely reflects his short tenure.
